parsed.doc_summary: Mirror of Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6 (updated Jan. 1, 2026): caps tenant application screening fees at $30 per applicant (CPI-adjusted), with conditions on charging, refunds, receipts and credit report copies. No official 2026 dollar figure is stated.

rules.title: California application screening fee limits
rules.requirement: Landlords may charge an application screening fee no greater than actual out-of-pocket costs and time, capped at $30 per applicant (adjusted annually for CPI since 1998). No fee if no unit is or will be available; fee requires first-come screening or full refund for unselected applicants; landlord must give an itemized receipt, refund unused amounts, and give the applicant a copy of the credit report within 7 days.
rules.quoted_span: In no case shall the amount of the application screening fee charged by the landlord or their agent be greater than thirty dollars ($30) per applicant.
rules.effective_date_note: Document says the section was updated Jan. 1, 2026 but does not give the date the core cap first took effect.
rules.interaction: Applies notwithstanding Civ. Code § 1950.5; fee is not treated as security under § 1950.5.
rules.conflict_note: The $30 base is CPI-adjusted annually; the document gives no single official 2026 dollar figure.
